8 June
On this day in 1707

The succession battle for Delhi throne was fought among Aurangzeb’s sons, Tara Azam and Bahadur Shah

Guru Gobind Singh helped Bahadhur Shah in this battle.

8 June brings together seven moments of Sikh history, from 1707 to 1984. The main event of the day is from 1707: The succession battle for Delhi throne was fought among Aurangzeb’s sons, Tara Azam and Bahadur Shah. Together they span four periods, from Guru Gobind Singh Ji and the Khalsa (1675–1708) to From the Anandpur Sahib Resolution to 1984 (1967–1984). People, places and movements connected with this day include Guru Gobind Singh Ji, Mughal rulers and governors, Delhi and the Akali movement and its morchas.

  • 1984Operation Woodrose started Sikh youth from villages picked up and eliminated. MacCarthy style witch hunt led to killing of hundreds of Sikhs and arrest of thousands of Sikhs.

Historical background

Guru Gobind Singh Ji and the Khalsa (1675–1708)

Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was executed in Delhi in 1675 on Aurangzeb's orders, and his son Guru Gobind Singh Ji became the tenth Guru at the age of nine. From Anandpur and Paonta he led the Sikhs through conflicts with the hill rajas and Mughal governors, created the Khalsa at Vaisakhi in 1699, and in the battles of 1704–1705 lost all four Sahibzade. Before his death at Nanded in 1708 he vested Guruship in the Guru Granth Sahib and the Khalsa Panth.

On this day in this period: 1707 The succession battle for Delhi throne was fought among Aurangzeb’s sons, Tara Azam and….

The Gurdwara Reform (Akali) movement (1920–1925)

Sikhs organised the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (November 1920) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (December 1920) to free historic gurdwaras from hereditary mahants backed by the government. Through non-violent morchas, including Nankana Sahib (1921), the keys agitation (1921–22), Guru ka Bagh (1922) and Jaito (1923–25), and alongside the militant Babbar Akali movement, the campaign led to the Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925.

On this day in this period: 1924 Waryam Singh of Dhugga was killed at Chak No.

The Punjabi Suba movement (1948–1966)

In independent India the Akali Dal campaigned for a Punjabi-speaking state, the Punjabi Suba, through repeated morchas led by Master Tara Singh and Sant Fateh Singh. The demand was met with the reorganisation of Punjab on 1 November 1966, which created present-day Punjab, Haryana and transferred hill areas to Himachal Pradesh.

On this day in this period: 1956 Gian Singh Rarewala announced his intention to join Congress.

From the Anandpur Sahib Resolution to 1984 (1967–1984)

The Akali Dal adopted the Anandpur Sahib Resolution in 1973 and launched the Dharam Yudh Morcha in 1982 over river waters, Chandigarh and greater state autonomy. Tensions culminated in Operation Blue Star, the Indian Army's assault on the Darbar Sahib complex in June 1984, the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on 31 October 1984 and the anti-Sikh violence in Delhi and elsewhere that followed.

On this day in this period: 1981 Secret meeting of Akali Dal where strong opinions were expressed for Khalsitan; 1984 Sirdar Khushwant Singh returned his "Padam Sri" in protest of Indian army’s attack on…; 1984 Giani Zail Singh, President of India, visits Darbar Sahib, Amritsar, after Indian Amry’s…; 1984 Operation Woodrose started.

People and places of this day

Guru Gobind Singh Ji

The tenth Guru (1666–1708), born at Patna. He created the Khalsa in 1699, led the Sikhs through the battles of Anandpur, Chamkaur and Muktsar, composed works collected in the Dasam Granth, and before his death at Nanded vested Guruship in the Guru Granth Sahib.

Read more → · Mentioned on 34 other days of the year

Mughal rulers and governors

The Mughal emperors Jahangir and Aurangzeb ordered the executions of Guru Arjan Dev Ji and Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, and Aurangzeb's successors and the governors of Lahore and Sirhind, among them Wazir Khan, Zakariya Khan and Mir Mannu, led the long campaign against the Sikhs between 1704 and the 1750s.

Mentioned on 34 other days of the year

Delhi

The Mughal capital, where Guru Har Krishan Ji died (Gurdwara Bangla Sahib), Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was executed (Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib) and Banda Singh Bahadur was put to death in 1716. Baghel Singh's forces entered the city in 1783 and marked its Sikh sites.

Read more → · Mentioned on 52 other days of the year

The Akali movement and its morchas

The Gurdwara Reform movement of 1920–1925, in which jathas of Akali volunteers non-violently took control of historic gurdwaras from mahants. Its campaigns included the keys morcha, Guru ka Bagh and Jaito; tens of thousands were arrested and hundreds killed or injured before the Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925. The Shiromani Akali Dal has remained the main Sikh political party.

Mentioned on 156 other days of the year

Sri Harmandir Sahib (Darbar Sahib)

The central Sikh shrine in Amritsar, built by Guru Arjan Dev Ji in the middle of the sacred pool, where the Adi Granth was installed in 1604. Destroyed by Ahmad Shah Abdali and rebuilt, it was covered in gold under Maharaja Ranjit Singh and has been at the centre of many events in Sikh history.

Read more → · Mentioned on 51 other days of the year

Amritsar

The city founded by Guru Ram Das Ji around the sacred pool of Amritsar. As the home of Sri Harmandir Sahib and the Akal Takht it has been the spiritual and political centre of the Sikhs for four centuries.

Read more → · Mentioned on 112 other days of the year

Operation Blue Star and November 1984

In June 1984 the Indian Army attacked the Darbar Sahib complex in Amritsar and some forty other gurdwaras to remove armed militants led by Sant Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale; many pilgrims were killed and the Akal Takht was heavily damaged. Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards on 31 October 1984, and thousands of Sikhs were killed in the violence that followed in Delhi and other cities.
